hints.title: Inclusion Exclusion Principle Area
hints.text: The total area covered by two rectilinear rectangles equals the sum of their individual areas minus the area of their mutual overlapping intersection.

hints.title: Projected Interval Overlap Invariant
hints.text: The overlapping width is the maximum of zero and the minimum of right edges minus the maximum of left edges; similarly for overlapping height.

hints.title: Bounding Box Overlap Calculation Procedure
hints.text: Calculate individual areas of both rectangles. Compute overlapping width by taking min(ax2, bx2) minus max(ax1, bx1) clamped at zero. Compute overlapping height by taking min(ay2, by2) minus max(ay1, by1) clamped at zero. Return sum of individual areas minus product of overlapping width and height.

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Grid simulation or point-by-point counting incurs astronomical memory and time overhead for large coordinate bounds.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using elementary geometry and clamping takes O(1) arithmetic operations and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should correctly apply the inclusion-exclusion principle and clamp overlapping dimension spans to zero when disjoint.
